data.title: Larry McDonald survived Lehman's collapse. Now he warns the credit market is signaling a growth shock for stocks.
data.description:
By Michael Sincere

Bear Traps Report founder explains why he sees stagflation coming, how much AI risk sits in S&P 500 index funds and why he favors hard assets

"Everybody's in growth stocks, and nobody's in value. Value stocks are going to crush growth in the coming years," says Larry McDonald.

Larry McDonald was a vice president at Lehman Brothers when the firm collapsed in 2008. Now he says he sees a record wave of convertible-bond issuance - a warning sign he saw before Lehman fell - along with a move into consumer staples and credit markets that are shutting off financing for artificial intelligence.

McDonald is the founder of "The Bear Traps Report" and the New York Times bestselling author of "A Colossal Failure of Common Sense" and "How to Listen When Markets Speak."

In this recent interview, edited for length and clarity, McDonald shares what the credit market is telling stock investors, how much AI risk sits in S&P 500 SPX index funds, which hard assets he favors, whether gold and silver are still worth buying, how investors nearing retirement can defend their portfolios and what younger investors should watch.

MarketWatch: Is there something the market is telling you that investors are missing?

McDonald: Definitely. Look at S&P [500] growth expectations for earnings next year. They're viciously high. But if you look at consumer staples (stocks of companies that sell everyday necessities, such as Walmart (WMT)) versus discretionary, consumer staples are outperforming by almost 19% in the last six months. The high-yield bond market hasn't been able to rally at all. The neoclouds (companies that rent out AI computing power) are all blowing up, and there's a big default coming there.

If you listen to the consumer staples and you listen to the bond market, all of it points to a major growth shock. That's where earnings are going to come down hard.

MarketWatch: Is the risk of a credit crisis gone, delayed or ahead of us?

McDonald: As you can see with the neoclouds, it's clearly starting again. The bulls say it's not 2000 because there's endless demand for computing power. But the only way you get endless demand is if there's endless financing and easy money. The capital markets are basically shutting off the financing for AI right now. That's what's causing the growth shock.

'The only way you get endless demand for computing power is if there's endless financing and easy money.'Larry McDonald

MarketWatch: When people buy an S&P 500 index fund, do they realize how much AI risk they are taking?

McDonald: It's pure evil. If Jack Bogle was alive right now, he would be sick to his stomach.

Ten years ago, the top two stocks in the S&P were 5% of the index. As of this month, the top two stocks are Nvidia (NVDA) and Apple (AAPL). Most investors have no idea that if they have $1 million in an S&P 500 index fund, $150,000 is in two stocks. Ten years ago, it would have been $50,000.

MarketWatch: How close is the U.S. to 1970s-style stagflation, and are investors prepared for it?

McDonald: In the '70s, that level of stagflation was a 10, which was the worst. We're not getting to that, because back then there was approximately 10% unemployment and approximately 8% inflation. But on a scale of 1 to 10, we're heading toward a 5, 6 or 7.

You don't read much about it, but everybody's in growth stocks, and nobody's in value. Value stocks are going to crush growth in the coming years. Think of the percentage of household wealth that's long hard assets, not just precious metals but copper, uranium and aluminum. In 1980, 5% or 6% of household wealth was long a lot of these commodities, and now it's less than 1%.

MarketWatch: Where would a regular investor go to buy hard assets?

McDonald: The whole AI trade for the next 20 years is going to need a lot more uranium. Sprott Physical Uranium Trust SRUUF is a really attractive commodity right now. Looking out the next three years, there's a meaningful deficit for uranium. The supply of uranium relative to global demand is going to be far short. I think that uranium prices could go up 100% to 200% in the coming years, potentially. Same thing with silver. You have a huge buildout in solar. Texas Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa is going to do a deal with the AI infrastructure companies, the data centers, and she's going to force them into a lot more solar.

We love First Solar (FSLR). We love iShares Silver Trust SLV. With the demand for silver that's going to come from AI, and the Fed potentially having to cut off the hiking cycle and not being able to hike too much, the setup for silver and solar is extremely bullish.

MarketWatch: Gold (GC00) and silver (SI00) both hit records earlier this year, and both have since fallen sharply. Are they still worth buying?

McDonald: Silver is the industrial metal, and consumer staples have been outperforming discretionary. There's a lot of people that are worried about a slowdown. Silver's approximately 60% off the highs. That's a really bullish setup because it's already priced in a lot of the industrial pain.

On the gold side, interest on the [national] debt is $1.1 trillion, and the Fed's not going to be able to hike too much more because if they were to hike 75 basis points, interest on the debt goes to nearly $1.3 trillion. We're coming into a stagflationary environment. That's really bullish for gold.

MarketWatch: Does bitcoin (BTCUSD) belong in someone's portfolio?

McDonald: Yes. You want to track the bitcoin-gold ratio (the number of ounces of gold that one bitcoin buys). When it's in the 30s, you want to sell bitcoin and buy gold. When it gets down into 12 to 17, you want to sell some gold and buy some bitcoin.

The big problem is when you go risk-off and the VIX VIX (the market's volatility gauge) is high. Unfortunately, being long bitcoin is similar to being short the VIX. There's a lot of weak hands in bitcoin, a lot of tourists. If we go risk-off with a high VIX and the markets are down 20%, bitcoin has really suffered every time, whereas gold has been a much, much better store of value.

'Being long bitcoin is similar to being short the VIX.'Larry McDonald

MarketWatch: Over the next 12 to 24 months, what are the best opportunities that investors are overlooking?

McDonald: We love Nike (NKE) heading into the 2028 Summer Olympics. It's trading below the 200-month moving average. The capitulation score in our model was one of the greatest signals we've ever seen. If you buy Nike this far below the 200-month moving average, your probability of making money in the coming years is very, very high.

Century Aluminum (CENX) is one of our highest-conviction ideas. It's a $3 billion market cap, so it's not a big company, but we think they're going to do $1 billion of free cash flow next year. That's a 30% free-cash-flow yield. It offers investors a decent amount of protection because they're buying back stock. I think your downside is approximately 10% or 20%, but your upside is 200%.

MarketWatch: How can readers who are nearing retirement and own S&P 500 index funds defend their portfolios against a high-inflation environment?

McDonald: The first thing you want to do is call your financial adviser and have them recreate the S&P 500 with a higher weighting toward industrials, materials and energy. It should be illegal to have 50% of your S&P in tech and AI, and that's essentially where we're going to be pretty soon.

MarketWatch: Any recommendations for readers in their 20s and 30s?

McDonald: No. 1, it's a wonderful time to be a young investor because the amount of information you can get from podcasts is like reading hundreds of books. It's incredible.

I think the biggest thing for younger people is to understand how dislocated the market is historically. Whenever one sector gets too big - like in 2000, tech was too big. In 2008, financials were too big. In 2013, oil and gas were too big. Now technology (and communication services combined) is almost 45% of the S&P, and they're adding these crazy IPOs - Anthropic (ANT), OpenAI and SpaceX (SPCX). You want to always beware of when one sector gets too big, and you want to go the other way.

MarketWatch: What warning signs did you see before Lehman collapsed that investors can learn from today?

McDonald: The convertible-bond market (bonds that can be exchanged for stock) is the best leading indicator. Whenever you see an explosion of convertible-bond issuance, and we just went to a record, that means these neoclouds, there's eight of them - they have been shut out of the high-yield bond market. This is another thing we saw before Lehman and the dot-com [bust]. They've been forced into what we call the last saloon. The last saloon is the convertible-bond market.

MarketWatch: How does today compare with Lehman?

McDonald: Far more wealth is at risk to inflation and interest rates. It's a lot worse, because today, household ownership of equities is at record levels. There's a lot more wealth as a percentage of household wealth. Equities are bigger today than 2007. But when Lehman went down, bonds gave you lots of protection.

The problem today is that the deficits are so high and the irresponsibility in Washington is off the charts in terms of deficit spending that, if the stock market gets hit, the bonds aren't going to offer you the same type of protection. This could be, in a lot of ways, a lot worse than Lehman.

MarketWatch: Is there anything else you see that most investors are missing?

data.title: All Aboard! Spend the Holidays with Trains at the Museum of Science
data.description:
All Aboard! Spend the Holidays with Trains at the Museum of Science

Now in its 9th year and bigger than ever, the Museum’s beloved holiday tradition brings miniature Boston landmarks, holiday films, and family fun for every generation

A beloved Museum of Science holiday tradition has pulled into the station. The ninth annual All Aboard! Trains at Science Park is now open through January 18, 2027, inviting guests of all ages to explore intricate miniature train displays featuring snow-covered peaks, colorful landscapes, and detailed scenes complete with décor, buildings, and tiny townsfolk. Model trains of various scales power along their tracks through meticulously crafted settings, making the exhibit a festive outing for families and friends of all ages throughout the season.

Every turn of the track brings something fun, including a miniature Boston that locals will love. Trains wind past the Prudential Center, Fenway Park and the Kenmore T stop, cross the iconic Zakim Bridge, and even pull up to a to-scale model of the Museum of Science itself. Beyond the city limits, they climb through towering mountain scenes and cozy winter villages. Expert model train makers handcrafted each scene, down to the last tiny tree.

By the Numbers

  • ~600 feet of model railroad track
  • ~800 model trees
  • 200+ miniature streetlights
  • 1,920 square feet of fake snow

Hands-On Fun for Every Generation
Visitors can also "drive" a train through a snowy mountain scene, discover trains from around the world, and compose their own symphony using train sounds and musical elements. Little engineers will love the expanded play area, with wooden train tables and a design-a-train activity, while parents and grandparents are just as likely to be found lingering over the details. All Aboard! Trains at Science Park is presented in English and Spanish and is included with Exhibition Halls admission.

The Holidays on the Big Screen and Under the Dome
Also beginning November 21, the Museum's theaters will offer even more ways to celebrate the season:

  • Mugar Omni Theater: Train Time, a captivating film that pairs naturally with the exhibit
  • 4-D Theater: the holiday classic Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer 4-D
  • Charles Hayden Planetarium: the return of God, Science, and Our Search for Meaning, written and narrated by international bestselling author Dan Brown

Tickets for Train Time, Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer 4-D, and God, Science, and Our Search for Meaning are available as admission add-ons. Visit https://www.mos.org/trains-winter-holiday-exhibit for more.

More Ways to Celebrate the Season
Give the Gift of Wonder: a Museum of Science membership is a great gift for curious minds of any age. It opens the door to a year filled with moments that spark wonder, like watching dancing robots, seeing a lightning storm indoors, and talking with a real-life space explorer. Members enjoy a year of unlimited visits, special discounts, exclusive events, and more. Visit https://www.mos.org/join/gift-memberships for more.

The fun extends well beyond the train tracks. Festive photo opportunities can be found inside All Aboard! and throughout the Museum, and the Museum Store, onsite and online, is stocked with gifts of wonder for everyone on your list.

All Aboard! Trains at Science Park was made possible through a collaboration with the Hub Division, Inc., of the Northeast Region (NER) of the National Model Railroad Association (NMRA).

About the Museum of Science
The Museum of Science is one of the world’s leading science centers, with a mission to inspire a lifelong love of science in everyone. The Museum’s 2030 ambition: two million visitors onsite, three million learners in schools, one billion people online annually. Together, these goals will expand access to evidence-based science and spark curiosity far beyond the Museum's walls, to classrooms and communities around the world. Its newest space, the William and Charlotte Bloomberg Public Science Common, brings the public and science together in Boston and beyond.

Additional assets can be found in the press kit here.

data.title: How a brutal week for stocks almost wiped out their gains for the entire year
data.description:
By Joy Wiltermuth and Claudia Assis

Investors are now more focused on protecting their portfolios than looking for bargains

Fear on Wall Street is running high as the Nasdaq swings to a yearly loss and the Dow and S&P 500 give back most of their 2026 gains.

There wasn't much left of the stock market's earlier robust gains for 2026 after Friday's carnage.

Investors dumped artificial-intelligence beneficiaries Nvidia (NVDA), Sandisk (SNDK) and Micron (MU), alongside defensive stocks like Costco (COST), leaving few areas of the market unscathed ahead of the holiday-shortened Thanksgiving week.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average DJIA closed below the 50,000 threshold for a second straight day, joining the S&P 500 index SPX and Nasdaq Composite COMP in at least a 10% correction from their previous record closes.

Under the surface, things looked even more dire. A tally on Friday showed that 64% of the S&P 500's constituents closed at least 20% below their record highs, according to Dow Jones Market Data. That figure reached as high as 87% for the battered information-technology sector.

The S&P 500's information-technology sector has all but a sliver of its constituents down 20% or more from their record highs

"We are in the midst of a re-evaluation and a correction," said Jim Caron, chief investment officer of portfolio solutions at Morgan Stanley Investment Management.

Earnings and the economy still look good for next year, Caron said. But anxiety has only grown around the artificial-intelligence trade, especially with new scrutiny in Washington into sales of Nvidia's chips to China. There's also the U.S. midterm elections, which exposed how deeply unpopular the data-center boom has been with voters.

"It's not just about circular financing," Caron said, nor concerns about the speed of returns on AI investments. It's also a bigger conversation about how to build data centers in communities in a more sustainable and durable way. "We can't have a data center go in and everyone's electricity bill goes up," he added.

The hope was that Nvidia's stellar earnings and Anthropic's (ANT) historic IPO would staunch the bleeding this week in markets. And there was hope that investors might take heart in the economy's resilience and start picking through the stock-market carnage for bargains.

Instead, as of Friday the S&P 500 was up only 1% for the year, while the Dow was 0.2% higher and the Nasdaq was down 2.7%, according to FactSet.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq-100 NDX was down 0.9% for the year, off more than 19% from its record high and on the cusp of a bear market.

Into the void

"It's a buyers' strike, even though we now have lower valuations," said Keith Lerner, chief investment officer at Truist Advisory Services. There's also little clarity on what the next catalysts could be to shift sentiment back to a more positive direction, he said.

Stocks staged a dramatic rebound after President Donald Trump's April 9, 2025, pause on most of his reciprocal tariffs, as feverish dip-buying quickly erased the fallout in financial markets. The same pattern repeated several times during the first part of Trump's second term in the White House.

But with the "blue wave" soon putting control of the House and Senate in the hands of Democrats, Wall Street no longer expects an executive order or a social-media post that can shift market sentiment in an instant.

Is the AI punchbowl gone?

Investors have begun treating the midterm results as the moment the punchbowl was removed from the AI party.

"The midterms got rid of the assumption that there won't be pushback against data centers," said Keith Buchanan, a fund manager at Globalt Investments. "It made that part of it real."

As part of this, valuations in the stock market have come down dramatically. The S&P 500's information-technology sector was trading at a forward price-to-earnings ratio of 16.3, based on Thursday's close, which was the lowest since the March 2020 COVID crisis, according to John Butters, a senior earnings analyst at FactSet. That's down from a 22 ratio at the beginning of 2026.

"This is almost like an epic rethink of the sector," said Truist's Lerner. "What it tells me is that people have lost confidence in the earnings outlook."

Wall Street now expects peak earnings growth this year, but for the S&P 500 to still see 16% to 17% earnings growth next year. But comments from Federal Reserve governor Christopher Waller suggest the 2027 backdrop could be less business-friendly. He's been at the forefront in warning that a "shock" may be needed to coax inflation back down to the central bank's 2% annual target.

The Fed's next decision on rates is Dec. 9, with the odds favoring back-to-back rate hikes through January, according to the CME FedWatch Tool.

Investors worry the Fed could tighten financial conditions too much and damage the economy.

The gloom hasn't improved even though global oil prices (BRN00) have tumbled almost 20% so far in November. Instead, Wall Street's "fear gauge" has surged more than 50% over the same stretch, with the below chart showing the Cboe Volatility Index VIX jump's above 30 on Friday.

When the "VIX" spikes, it implies there will be increased volatility in the S&P 500 over the next 30 days. That backdrop suggests investors might be more focused on protecting their portfolios, rather than looking to buy cheaper stocks.

As Caron at Morgan Stanley put it, "What's left over is the emotional aspect of preserving gains for the year."

Mike DeStefano contributed

-Joy Wiltermuth -Claudia Assis

SAN DIEGO, Nov. 20, 2026

SAN DIEGO, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Shareholder rights law firm Robbins LLP reminds investors that a class action was filed on behalf of all persons who purchased or otherwise acquired Kinross Gold Corporation (NYSE: KGC) common stock between February 18, 2026 and September 23, 2026, inclusive (the "Class Period"). Kinross is a Canadian gold mining company headquartered in Toronto Ontario with regional offices and mining facilities in the United States and abroad.

The complaint alleges that Kinross concealed the Company's inability to meet production benchmarks.  

Investors who purchased Kinross Gold Corporation common stock during the Class Period and suffered significant losses should contact Robbins LLP for information about the lawsuit before January 5, 2027.

Why Was Kinross Sued?

According to the complaint, during the Class Period, defendants created the false impression that they possessed reliable information pertaining to the Company's projected production outlook and anticipated growth while also minimizing risk from continued sequential production declines from Round Mountain Phase S. In truth, Kinross' repeated optimistic claims of a strong production ramp in the second half of 2026 sufficient to meet the attributable production guidance management had provided fell short of reality. The Company was simply not equipped to meet production benchmarks without slowing the rate of ore recovery.

Why Did Kinross Stock Drop?

On September 23, 2026, Kinross issued an "Operational and Return of Capital Update" mid-quarter. In the release, Kinross announced that both full-year 2026 and 2027 attributable production guidance was being reduced to 1.84 million to 1.86 million Au eq. oz. The Company attributed the results, in significant part, on ore recovery challenges at Round Mountain. Defendants would later disclose these challenges were operational in nature and were likely to stem from dilution caused by the use of oversized tools and machinery in the mining process.

On this news, the price of Kinross' common stock declined from a closing market price of $27.62 per share on September 23, 2026, to $24.42 per share on September 24, 2026, a decline of about 11.5% in the span of just a single day.

What Can Kinross Investors Do Now?

Investors who purchased lululemon athletica inc. securities during the Class Period may be eligible to serve as lead plaintiff. The lead plaintiff is a court-appointed investor who represents the interests of all class members throughout the litigation. Shareholders who wish to seek appointment as lead plaintiff should contact Robbins LLP for information about the appointment process before January 5, 2027.

Shareholders do not need to serve as lead plaintiff to share in any potential recovery. Those who do not seek appointment may remain absent class members.

Does It Cost Anything to Participate?

No. Robbins LLP represents investors on a contingency fee basis, with no upfront or out-of-pocket fees or expenses.

Contact Robbins LLP

Investors seeking additional information about the Kinross Gold Corporation scurities class action may contact Robbins LLP by submitting an inquiry, emailing attorney Aaron Dumas, Jr., or calling (800) 350-6003.

Why Robbins LLP?

A recognized leader in shareholder rights litigation, Robbins LLP represents investors in securities fraud and shareholder derivative litigation. We have helped restore more than $2 billion in value to shareholders and secured some of the largest recoveries in shareholder derivative litigation history. 

"Companies have an obligation to provide investors with complete and accurate information so that markets can function fairly and efficiently," said Brian J. Robbins, Founding Partner of Robbins LLP.

Lost Money in Backward Hat Capital (BH Capital)? Gibbs Mura is Investigating Potential Legal Claims on Behalf of BH Capital Investors

Gibbs Mura and Silver Law Group are investigating potential legal claims on behalf of people who invested in Backward Hat Capital (“BH Capital”) or its affiliated funds, including Traders Point Capital and AI Capital. Federal authorities allege the firm ran a foreign exchange Ponzi scheme that raised more than $600 million from over 2,000 investors. The potential Backward Hat Capital Class Action Lawsuit aims to help investors to recover losses.

What is the Backward Hat Capital Legal Investigation About?

According to federal prosecutors in the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of New York and civil enforcement filings by the Securities and Exchange Commission and Commodity Futures Trading Commission, Backward Hat Capital operated as a collection of funds founded around 2022 that marketed foreign exchange trading via a proprietary algorithm. Investors were purportedly promised returns typically exceeding 6% per month.

Federal authorities allege that:

  • Backward Hat did not conduct forex trading as represented to investors, putting only minimal funds toward actual forex trading;
  • More than $200 million in incoming investor money was used to pay redemptions to existing investors, while withdrawal requests were increasingly delayed or stalled with shifting transfer excuses;
  • Hundreds of millions of dollars were transferred to insiders and related entities, including more than $130 million to co-founder Phillip Patrick Williams and more than $40 million to co-founder Devin Allen Johnson; and
  • Purported “independent” financial audit and quality-of-earnings reports were prepared by Joseph Anderson without genuine audit work or true independence, despite undisclosed financial ties and expected payouts to the auditor.

According to the SEC complaint, Backward Hat funds include:

  • Backward Hat Capital Fund LP
  • BH Capital Fund I LP
  • BH Capital Fund IV LP
  • BH Capital Fund VIII LP
  • BH Capital Fund IX LP
  • BH Capital Fund X LP
  • BH Capital Fund XX LP

VistaPrint Partners with Acclaimed Restaurateurs Sohla and Ham El-Waylly for Opening of Brooklyn’s Triangle Bar

From custom deli paper to coasters and menus, VistaPrint is helping bring Fort Greene’s newest neighborhood bar to life

VistaPrint, the print and design partner to millions of small businesses, today announced a partnership with award-winning chefs and culinary personalities, Sohla and Ham El-Waylly, to support the opening of their newest Brooklyn venture, Triangle Bar. Additional Triangle Bar partners include Anoop Pillarisetti and Michael Tuiach.

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261120304334/en/

VistaPrint Partners with Acclaimed Restaurateurs Sohla and Ham El-Waylly for Opening of Brooklyn’s Triangle Bar

Located at the base of Fort Greene’s iconic triangular Fowler Square and opening in winter 2026–27, Triangle Bar is reimagining the classic neighborhood bar as a welcoming, all-occasion gathering place. The husband-and-wife duo invite guests to settle in over a pint, enjoy a comforting dinner, or linger over drinks with friends. The bar sits alongside the group’s Brooklyn restaurant, Strange Delight, a critically acclaimed, New Orleans-inspired seafood restaurant and cocktail bar in Fort Greene.

Sohla and Ham partnered with VistaPrint early in the planning process to create a consistent look and feel across every customer-facing touchpoint, including custom-printed sandwich deli paper, signature coasters, menus, takeout packaging and branded signage, t-shirts and hats.

"So much hard work goes into building a small business. Using custom print products is essential when you're trying to build an identity people remember, and we wanted every detail at Triangle Bar to feel intentional,” said Sohla and Ham El-Waylly. “When we opened Strange Delight, coordinating orders across multiple vendors while maintaining quality was exhausting. Having VistaPrint as our one-stop shop for all things branding completely streamlined the process. We're so excited to share Triangle Bar with the Fort Greene community.”

The partnership reflects VistaPrint’s ongoing commitment to championing food and beverage entrepreneurs by providing cohesive, high-quality marketing that turn brands into community destinations from opening day and beyond.

“Sohla and Ham are two of the culinary world’s most trusted voices, embodying the creativity and resilience required to build something completely their own,” said Heather Deschenes, Vice President, North America Marketing at VistaPrint. “Food and beverage branding and marketing live in tangible details that guests interact with every day. By serving as an end-to-end partner for Triangle Bar, VistaPrint makes it easy for entrepreneurs to bring their vision to life.”

For more information about the partnership and to explore the products used for the opening of Triangle Bar, click here.

About VistaPrint

VistaPrint is the print and design partner to millions of small businesses and households around the world. We help small business owners bring their ideas to life through custom print products, easy-to-use digital tools and expert design support. VistaPrint is a Cimpress company (Nasdaq: CMPR).

QuidelOrtho Investigation Initiated: Kahn Swick & Foti, LLC Investigates the Officers and Directors of QuidelOrtho Corporation - QDEL

QuidelOrtho Investigation Initiated: Kahn Swick & Foti, LLC Investigates the Officers and Directors of QuidelOrtho Corporation - QDEL

PR Newswire

NEW ORLEANS, Nov. 20, 2026

NEW ORLEANS, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Former Attorney General of Louisiana, Charles C. Foti, Jr., Esq., a partner at the law firm of Kahn Swick & Foti, LLC ("KSF"), announces that KSF has commenced an investigation into QuidelOrtho Corporation ("QuidelOrtho" or the "Company") (NasdaqGS: QDEL).

According to a securities class action filed against the Company, internal reports and accounts from former employees described serious and unresolved problems with the Company's flagship test, the Savanna Respiratory Viral Panel 4 ("RVP4"). The lawsuit alleges that the European launch was plagued by high rates of invalid test results, device failures, and mounting customer complaints, with between 60% and 80% of European customer feedback being negative. The complaint further alleges that Savanna's invalid test rate ran between 10% and 30%, far above the industry standard of 1% to 2%, and that roughly one in four instruments sold in Europe had to be replaced. According to the lawsuit, the product could not consistently meet the FDA's sensitivity requirements, and manufacturing yields fell far below internal targets, with former employees describing scrap rates of 50% to 80%. The lawsuit also alleges that the Company doubled its endemic COVID-19 revenue guidance, from $150 million–$200 million to $200 million–$400 million, without supporting data, even as internal reports showed declining sales and accumulating inventory.

KSF's investigation is focusing on whether QuidelOrtho's officers and/or directors of  breached their fiduciary duties to its shareholders or otherwise violated state or federal laws. 

If you have information that would assist KSF in its investigation, or have been a long-term holder of QuidelOrtho's shares and would like to discuss your legal rights, you may, without obligation or cost to you, call toll-free at 1-833-538-3606 or email KSF Managing Partner Lewis Kahn (lewis.kahn@ksfcounsel.com), or visit https://www.ksfcounsel.com/cases/nasdaqgs-qdel to learn more.
